evidence.claim: A plain corridor with repeated doors supports lower-tier movement.
Portable beds and tables create a temporary treatment or examination area.
A plain floor corridor allows several people to stand apart and pass.
A tall plain doorway forms a controlled room threshold.
A large room accommodates multiple folding beds and standing staff.
A circular gathering arrangement occupies a broad interior floor.
A large group moves together through an interior route.
Exposed overhead services and plain wall surfaces mark a lower-tier corridor class.
An exterior horizon panel confirms the ongoing voyage.

contradictionsAndQuarantines.subject: Medical or examination furniture
contradictionsAndQuarantines.rule: Portable examination furniture is a temporary room-use state, not fixed architecture.

contradictionsAndQuarantines.subject: Lower-tier route continuity
contradictionsAndQuarantines.rule: Separate corridor and crowd scenes establish room classes but not a continuous mapped route.
